_comment: Default (English) manifest strings. Korean lives in package.nls.ko.json. VS Code substitutes %key% throughout package.json at load time; source strings must stay here rather than inline so the two locales cannot drift apart silently.
welcome.noFolder:
TaskHub runs actions defined per project.
[Open Folder](command:vscode.openFolder)
Once a folder is open you can create actions in its .vscode/actions.json.
welcome.noActions:
No actions yet.
[Create Action](command:taskhub.createAction)
Or start from a sample and edit it by hand:
[Browse Examples](command:taskhub.showExampleJsonQuickPick)
[Import Actions…](command:taskhub.importActions)
welcome.noLinks:
No workspace links yet.
Links are shortcuts to docs, dashboards, or issue trackers, stored in .vscode/links.json.
[Add Link](command:taskhub.addLink)
welcome.noFavorites:
No favorite files yet.
Pin files you keep coming back to — right-click a file in the Explorer, or add one here.
[Add File to Favorites](command:taskhub.addFavoriteFile)
cmd.revealSymbolInMemoryMap: Memory Map: Reveal Symbol Under Cursor
setting.showTaskStatus: Master switch for action run feedback: status icons and progress in the Actions view, action-defined completion messages, and long-running completion cues. Turning this off **also silences failure notifications** (including an action's own `failMessage`) — check the History panel or the TaskHub output channel instead. Stopping actions is unaffected: the inline stop button and *Stop All Actions* stay available.
setting.backgroundCompletionThreshold: Minimum action duration in seconds before TaskHub shows a short completion status and may send a notification. `0` includes every action. `taskhub.showTaskStatus` remains the master switch.
setting.backgroundCompletionMode: Controls notifications for long-running successful or stopped actions. Detailed failure alerts remain individual so their action name and cause are not lost. The short status-bar cue still appears when this is `never`.
setting.backgroundCompletionMode.whenUnf: Notify successful or stopped actions only when the VS Code window was not focused as the action finished.
setting.backgroundCompletionMode.always: Notify successful or stopped actions whether or not the VS Code window was focused.
setting.backgroundCompletionMode.never: Do not send additional successful/stopped completion notifications; keep the short status-bar cue and detailed failure alerts.
setting.backgroundCompletionOutcomes: Terminal outcomes eligible for long-running completion cues: `success`, `failure`, and/or `stopped`. Status cues within 750 ms are collapsed into one summary; notifications collapse successful and stopped outcomes only, while failures keep their detailed alert. Use an empty array to disable these cues without changing other action feedback.
setting.showVerboseLogs: If true, shows detailed logs in the output panel when executing a pipeline. By default, only minimal status messages are shown.
setting.runLogsEnabled: Persist structured action run logs inside the workspace at `.taskhub/logs/`. This is off by default because stdout/stderr can contain project data or credentials that TaskHub cannot identify. Known `password: true` inputs and their derived outputs are redacted; terminal-streamed and background one-shot output is recorded only as unavailable.
setting.runLogsMaxFiles: Maximum number of action run log files retained across this workspace. Rotation removes expired logs first, then the oldest files until this limit is met.
setting.runLogsRetentionDays: Delete action run logs older than this many days. Set to `0` to disable age-based deletion; count and total-size rotation still apply.
setting.runLogsMaxTotalSize: Maximum combined size in MB of action run log files across this workspace. Each individual log is also capped at 8 MB and explicitly marked when persisted output is truncated.
setting.pythonIoEncoding: Value to assign to the `PYTHONIOENCODING` environment variable for commands launched by TaskHub. Set to an empty string to avoid forcing an encoding or provide values such as `utf-8:ignore` for compatibility.
setting.windowsPowerShellEncoding: Controls PowerShell console output and `>`/`>>` file-redirection encoding on Windows. With `utf8`, Windows PowerShell 5.1 writes a BOM while PowerShell 7 does not. Use `system` to keep the current console code page for legacy tools that do not recognise UTF-8 (code page 65001).
setting.outputCaptureLimitMb: Maximum size (in megabytes) of command stdout/stderr captured into memory during a TaskHub action. When a command exceeds this limit it is terminated with an error to protect the VS Code extension host from OOM. Raise this value for pipelines that intentionally emit large logs, or turn off `passTheResultToNextTask` so the output streams to the terminal instead of being captured.
setting.totalOutputLimitMb: Maximum **combined** size (in megabytes) of all task results a single action keeps in memory. Task results stay resident until the action ends because a later task may reference `${earlierTask.stdout}`. `pipeline.outputCaptureLimitMb` caps one task; this caps the sum — without it, raising the per-task cap for a noisy build lets a handful of tasks reach gigabytes. Never falls below the per-task cap: if you allow 100 MB from one task, at least that much must fit. Exceeding it fails the action.
setting.maxParallelTasks: Maximum number of tasks that may run concurrently within a single action. Only tasks marked `parallel: true` are exempt from the implicit "wait for every preceding task" barrier; once exempt they still wait for their explicit `dependsOn` and any `${taskId.x}` auto-inferred dependencies before starting. Tasks without `parallel: true` always act as sync barriers regardless of `dependsOn`. The default `4` is conservative because embedded builds (linker / LTO stages) can each consume gigabytes of RAM — raise this on machines with more resources, or lower to `1` to force fully sequential execution.
setting.historyMaxItems: Maximum number of action history items to keep.
setting.recentLimit: Maximum number of recently-used actions shown at the top of `TaskHub: Run Any Action…`. Set to `0` to hide the *Recently used* section entirely. Stale IDs (deleted actions) are filtered out at display time, so the visible count may be smaller than this limit.
setting.historyShowPanel: Show or hide the History panel in the TaskHub sidebar.
setting.showSourceControlContextMenu: Show TaskHub preview/browser actions in the Source Control resource context menu. VS Code does not reliably expose file-extension context keys for SCM resources, so these menu items may appear for all changed files; TaskHub still validates the file extension before opening.
setting.builtinActions: Controls whether TaskHub's bundled example actions (`defaultButton.*` from the extension's `media/actions.json`) appear in the Actions view. `auto` (default) keeps them out of your project's action list — the empty-state view links to them instead, so an empty Actions panel offers 'Create Action' rather than two demo buttons.
setting.builtinActions.auto: Keep the bundled examples out of the action list; the empty-state view offers a 'Browse Examples' button instead.
setting.builtinActions.always: Always merge the bundled example actions into the list (behavior before 0.6.14).
setting.builtinActions.never: Keep them out of the list and hide the 'Browse Examples' button from the empty-state view too.
setting.rememberLastLocation: Reopen TaskHub file/folder dialogs at the location last used for the same purpose (Hex Viewer, JSON Editor, Memory Map, export/import, each `fileDialog`/`folderDialog` task, ...). When a dialog has never been used for that purpose, it inherits the location most recently used by any TaskHub dialog — so an action that picks a file and then a folder continues where you just were. When off, TaskHub picks no starting location at all and leaves it to VS Code, which applies its own default rules and the `files.dialog.defaultPath` setting. Note that save dialogs then lose their suggested file name too — VS Code offers no way to propose a name without also proposing a folder. A `defaultUri` written into an action JSON is still honoured either way.
setting.hoverNumberBase: Enable number base conversion hover tooltip for C/C++ files. Shows binary, decimal, and hexadecimal representations when hovering over numeric literals.
setting.bitOperationHover:
**[Experimental]** Show bit operation results in hover tooltips for C/C++ files.

Displays calculation results for:
- Variable operations: `value |= 0x80` (shows Before/After)
- Constant expressions: `1U << 5` (shows Left/Result)

**Supported patterns:**
- ✅ `value & 0xFF` (variable & literal)
- ✅ `1U << 5` (constant expressions)
- ❌ `a ^ b` (variable & variable - not supported)

⚠️ This feature is experimental and may change in future versions.
setting.presetSelected:
Select a preset to automatically apply predefined actions.

- **none**: Use only workspace actions
- **example**: Example preset with Git and Build commands
- Or enter a custom preset ID from extension or workspace `.vscode/presets/` folder

Presets are merged with workspace `.vscode/actions.json` (workspace actions take priority).
